summary.headline: EMS Ltd Q2 FY27 operating income Rs 160.89 crore, up ~30% YoY; EBITDA margin 22.26%, unexecuted order book Rs 3,152 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 operating income was Rs 160.89 crore, EBITDA Rs 35.82 crore, PBT Rs 30.72 crore and PAT Rs 22.92 crore, with management citing ~30% growth in operating income and ~50% growth in EBITDA and PAT versus Q1. Management attributed the weak prior-year base to a Uttarakhand monsoon disruption in FY26 that halted network sewer laying work for 2-3 months. Order inflow in the quarter was about Rs 900 crore from Jal boards (Delhi, PHED Rajasthan, UP Jal Nigam), taking unexecuted order book to Rs 3,152 crore as of 30 September 2026. Management guided to 30-35% sequential growth in Q3 and Q4, and said FY27 could match FY25 revenue, though no formal numeric guidance was given. Receivables delays in Uttarakhand (ADB/JICA-funded projects) and a central fund-flow portal change affected collections, now said to be normalised in UP.

vs Rs 355 crore in H1 FY26 (decline)

financial_highlights.value: ~Rs 60 crore, about 30% of earlier ~Rs 200 crore pledge
financial_highlights.change: Management says ~70% withdrawn; target zero this FY

segments.commentary: Rs 2,171 crore, about 85% of unexecuted order book; described as core business (water supply and sewage treatment).

segments.name: O&M (order book)

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q3 FY27 operating income about 30-35% above Q2, and Q4 about 30-35% above Q3.
Management said FY27 revenue could reach FY25 levels; FY26 was below FY25. No explicit numeric FY27 revenue, EBITDA or PAT guidance given.
Management expects EBITDA margin around 25% plus or minus 1% by year-end FY27, versus 22.26% in Q2.
Management targets a Rs 3,000 crore order book at all times and expects around 20% annual revenue CAGR over the next 2-3 years.
Management expects Rs 900 crore Q2 order to contribute little in FY27 because it takes 4-6 months to start work.
capex_capacity: No own capex planned beyond machinery; work is on government-funded (central/state/ULB) capex, per management.
Uttarakhand network sewer laying largely complete; remaining work is campus-based (STP/WTP), expected to be less affected by monsoon.
Management is bidding aggressively for about Rs 3,500 crore of projects next quarter and expects Rs 5,600 crore of new orders by December, per management statement.
Operating in 8-9 states; order book split: UP 35%, Rajasthan 27%, Uttarakhand 12%, Kolkata 12%, Bihar 3%, Mumbai 3%, MP 3.43%, Delhi 4%, Gujarat 1%, Haryana 1%.
demand_pricing: Unexecuted order book Rs 3,152 crore (excl. GST) as of 30 Sep 2026; Rs 2,619 crore capex and balance O&M; Rs 900 crore added in Q2 from Delhi Jal Board, PHED Rajasthan and UP Jal Nigam (Urban).
Revenue by state: UP 25%, Uttarakhand 67%, Maharashtra 6% (remainder small).
Management says margins are slightly better than peers, with competition rising and new entrants increasing.
Management said order book converts at roughly 40% per year; from Sept 2026 to Sept 2027 implied revenue about Rs 1,200 crore.
Receivables: Uttarakhand payments on ADB/JICA-funded projects slipped from 90-120 days to 2-3 months extra; UP payments normalised after central portal change (April-July disruption).

qa_highlights.question: How are collections from UP government, and what is the Uttarakhand receivable position?
qa_highlights.answer: UP has normalised after a central-to-state pro-rata funding portal change that disrupted flows April-July; Uttarakhand delays are longer on ADB/JICA funded projects. Management said part of ~Rs 450 crore receivables is over 6 months but includes unbilled amounts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book composition and execution timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 3,152 crore excl. GST; water and waste water 85%. About Rs 900 crore is L1 or LOA stage and not started; around Rs 1,600 crore under execution. Management said order book converts about 40% a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H1 FY27 revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a 2-3 month halt on Uttarakhand network works in the FY26 monsoon; H1 FY26 was Rs 355 crore versus Rs 286 crore in H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated revenue grow less than standalone and what drove higher other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the consolidated gap reflects a low-margin subsidiary (flax factory) running at 2-4% profit. Other expenses rose on project-based consultancy and soil exploration for new orders and are expected to ease.

qa_highlights.question: What mitigates monsoon risk in Uttarakhand?
qa_highlights.answer: Network laying is largely complete; remaining work is campus-based (STP/WTP) and less exposed to rain, though management said only a bit can be mitigated against unprecedented rainfall.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pledge position?
qa_highlights.answer: Pledge reduced from about Rs 200 crore to about Rs 60 crore; management aims to reach zero this financial year.

risks_watch: Monsoon exposure: FY26 Uttarakhand disruption cut revenue; mitigation depends on campus works being less exposed.
Receivables: Uttarakhand ADB/JICA payment delays and over-6-month balances within ~Rs 450 crore; watch collections and any provisioning.
Execution lag: Rs 900 crore Q2 order will not start for 4-6 months, so FY27 revenue growth depends on existing book.
Consolidated vs standalone gap: subsidiary earns thin margins; investors should track standalone numbers per management.
Other expenses increase in Q2 (project-related) and management said it is one-time; confirm normalisation in Q3.
Pledge of promoter shares (~30% of earlier pledge still outstanding) to be cleared this year.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on recovery and order book, but evasive and inconsistent on specific figures (order book O&M split, revenue guidance, consolidated numbers), with repeated answers on the Uttarakhand monsoon and receivables.
key_quotes: And in this quarter, we have got tremendous increase in our order book that is around Rs. 900 crores from different Jal boards like Delhi Jal board, PHED Rajasthan and UP Jal Nigam (Urban), Uttar Pradesh.
So, operating income is increasing by 30%, but our profits are increasing by 50%. So, profit margin is increasing.
There is no gap. Basically, in civil engineering, you cannot cut it like a chemical industry that day-to-day production is this much and day-to-day production is that much.

growth.why: Management guides Q3 and Q4 revenue each 30-35% above the prior quarter and says FY27 can match FY25 revenue (no numeric target), backed by a Rs 3,152 crore order book (Rs 900 crore added in Q2) and a Rs 3,000 crore book target, but the Rs 900 crore order takes 4-6 months to start and there is no own capacity expansion.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects EBITDA margin around 25% plus or minus 1% by year-end FY27, versus 22.26% in Q2 FY27, citing a slightly better-than-peer margin profile despite rising competition.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management says it is making no own capex beyond machinery and works only on government-funded capex, so no new physical capacity is planned in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides Q3 operating income 30-35% above Q2 (Rs 160.89 crore) and Q4 30-35% above Q3, with FY27 revenue able to match FY25, backed by a Rs 3,152 crore order book converting about 40% a year (~Rs 1,200 crore implied Sept 2026 to Sept 2027).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management explicitly says it is not making its own capex at all; utilisation is not disclosed, and work is on government-funded capex, so no company capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is bidding for about Rs 3,500 crore of projects next quarter and expects Rs 5,600 crore of new orders by December, which could lift the order book above the Rs 3,000 crore target, but the Rs 900 crore Q2 order takes 4-6 months to start and no numeric guidance was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables are stretched (~Rs 450 crore, part over 6 months, Uttarakhand ADB/JICA payments slipping by 2-3 months) and Uttarakhand monsoon risk persists on campus works, so the 30-35% sequential growth path could slip; FY27 guidance was already softened to 'match FY25' from no explicit number.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New products, brands or models were not discussed on the call.

rows.label: Receivables collection normalisation
rows.why: UP payments have normalised after the April-July central portal disruption, but ~Rs 450 crore receivables (part over 6 months, including unbilled) and Uttarakhand ADB/JICA delays of 2-3 extra months remain to be collected.

rows.label: Promoter pledge cleared to zero
rows.why: Pledge cut from about Rs 200 crore to about Rs 60 crore (~70% withdrawn), and management has committed to make it zero this financial year.

rows.label: Other expenses normalisation
rows.why: Q2 other expenses rose on project consultancy and soil exploration for new orders, which management called one-time and expects to ease, though this is not yet confirmed in numbers.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, Q3/Q4 sequential growth and pledge reduction, but was evasive and inconsistent on O&M order split, consolidated numbers and revenue guidance; analysts pressed on receivables, the Uttarakhand monsoon exposure and the H1 revenue decline.
